newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine '96 net grain harvest officially 26 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine '96 net grain harvest officially 26 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine's 1996 grain harvest is officially over and stands at a net 26 million tonnes, far below 1995's 36.5 million tonnes, the deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture said on Monday.
"We have gathered 26 million tonnes of grain this year, and we can export three million tonnes," Mykhailo Zubets told a news conference. "Most of the exports will be of winter wheat."
The net output figure was in line with what officials had said was expected from an extraordinarily difficult harvest.
But the result is one of the worst ever for the former Soviet republic, a one-time breadbasket of the region.
Ukraine needs about 10 million tonnes of grain a year for consumption by humans and livestock.
Zubets blamed the poor harvest on drought at the beginning of the growing season. But he said Ukraine planned to increase grain output in coming years.
"Our main goal in the agriculture sector is to return to the days when we produced from 47 to 50 million tonnes, in Soviet times," Zubets said.
He said winter wheat output stood at 13.0 million tonnes, down from 16.4 million tonnes a year ago.
"This year we have sown winter wheat at the optimum time. It is in a good state," he said. "We are now well into winter and there has been no damage."
Ukrainian weather forecasters are predicting a moist winter, several degrees above normal, he said.
"For us this is a good thing, since unexpected frosts could damage the young wheat," he said.
Winter wheat has traditionally been better suited to Ukraine's climate and moisture conditions than summer varieties.
Zubets also said the government planned to use more fertilisers next year to help grain crops.
